column2: That's exactly why the student loan scheme was created. Since May 2024, it has paid out over ₦375 billion across more than 1.6 million loans: tuition goes straight to the school, upkeep to the student. One UNILAG student said he was about to drop out before his loan paid his fees.
column3: NELFUND: ₦375.28bn across 1,675,474 loans. Admit some upkeep payments were delayed in July 2026.

column2: That rumour came from a statement the ICPC corrected: a missing word, "NOT", made it look like money was unaccounted for. No fraud by the fund was established. The investigation started because the fund itself reported schools making illegal deductions.
column3: ICPC correction of its April 2025 statement.

column2: Youth joblessness is serious, but the report behind that claim actually said 53%, not 80%. The bigger problem is underemployment: people working, but not earning enough. That's what programmes like 3MTT are aimed at.
column3: ActionAid/Plan International (2025). Official 15–24 rate: 6.5% (Q2 2024). 93% of workers are informal.

column1: “There are no jobs for young people.”
column2: That's a real problem. The 3MTT programme has trained over 135,000 people in tech skills, with 1.8 million in the pipeline, and LEEP is targeting 2.5 million jobs. I'd rather share results as they're published than oversell them.
column3: LEEP has no published placements yet; only 19% of 3MTT Cohort 1 completed.

column1: “Our doctors and nurses are all leaving.”
column2: That's true, and it's serious. In 2024 the government approved a policy to keep health workers and attract them back, and raised the retirement age to 65 so experienced staff can stay longer. More needs to be done.
column3: 3,974 doctors and 23,000+ nurses/midwives left in 2024. Acknowledge; don't deny.

column1: “Japa is proof this government has failed young people.”
column2: Many young people want to leave, and that hurts. But japa started long before this government: in 2022, polls found 69% of young Nigerians wanted to go. The fair question is what's being done now to keep them, like student loans and tech training.
column3: NBS: 34.5% of 20–30-year-olds want to migrate. Never repeat the "modern-day slavery" remark.

column1: Which youth programme must NOT be credited to Tinubu?
column2: The Youth Investment Fund: it began in 2020. Also never say japa is good because of remittances.
